# Enter, exit and origin (house standards, version 4)

<!-- generated by tools/build_data.py from synthesis/; edit the source, not this file -->

How things appear and leave: from a slightly smaller scale with opacity, out of their trigger, along the path they came in, in short staggers, with measured heights and clip-path reveals.

Rules from non-negotiable sources. **must**: never break it without the person's explicit override. **should**: the default; say so when you depart from it. How to change one: `../standards.md`.

### STD-enter-exit-origin-01: Never enter from scale(0)
**must**. Never animate an element in from scale(0) or out to scale(0); start from scale(0.9–0.97) together with opacity: 0, and use scale(0.95) + opacity: 0 as the replacement.
- Values: forbidden-start: scale(0); start-scale-range: 0.9–0.97; start-scale-min: 0.9; start-scale-default: 0.95; start-opacity: 0; article-demo-start-scale: 0.93
- Why: scale(0) looks like the element comes out of nowhere; nothing in the real world appears from nothing (or disappears and reappears completely), and a higher start scale is like a balloon, which keeps a visible shape even when deflated.
- `engine.py review` checks it: Never animate from scale(0): start from scale(0.95) with opacity: 0 (range 0.9–0.97).
- Sources: S-L19-003, S-L19-004, S-L19-018, S-L19-023, S-L19-033, S-L19-032, S-L19-025, S-L19-024, S-L19-016

### STD-enter-exit-origin-02: No opacity-only fade entrances
**must**. Give every entering element an initial transform (a slightly smaller scale or a small translate) alongside opacity: 0; do not ship opacity-only entrances. The sources show two exceptions: under prefers-reduced-motion keep the opacity and drop the transform, and a modal's backdrop fades with opacity alone.
- Values: entrance-start: opacity: 0 + transform: scale(0.95) (or a translate)
- Why: review-animations lists pure-fade entrances next to scale(0) as an escalation trigger to flag on sight, and the audit files them under physicality, whose premise is that nothing in the real world appears from nothing.
- Sources: S-L19-025, S-L19-032, S-L19-024, S-L19-017

### STD-enter-exit-origin-03: Scale popovers from their trigger
**must** · web, css, react. Set transform-origin to the trigger for popovers, dropdowns, menus, selects and tooltips so they scale out of the element that opened them, never from the default center (Base UI: transform-origin: var(--transform-origin); Radix dropdown: var(--radix-dropdown-menu-content-transform-origin)).
- Values: base-ui: transform-origin: var(--transform-origin); radix-dropdown-menu: transform-origin: var(--radix-dropdown-menu-content-transform-origin); forbidden: transform-origin: center on a trigger-anchored surface
- Why: The panel should look like it came out of the thing you clicked; CSS's default origin, center, is wrong for almost every popover, and anchoring content to its source makes the spatial relationship between button and content obvious.
- `engine.py review` checks it: Popovers, menus, dropdowns and tooltips scale from their trigger: transform-origin: var(--transform-origin).
- Sources: S-L19-003, S-L19-004, S-L19-018, S-L19-017, S-L19-023, S-L19-033, S-L19-032, S-L19-025, S-L19-024, S-L19-020

### STD-enter-exit-origin-04: Keep modals scaling from center
**must** · web, css, react. Keep modals at transform-origin: center; they are exempt from trigger-origin scaling and a centered modal is not a finding.
- Values: modal-transform-origin: center
- Why: Modals are not anchored to a specific trigger; they appear centered in the viewport.
- `engine.py review` checks it: Modals are not anchored to a trigger: keep transform-origin: center.
- Sources: S-L19-017, S-L19-018, S-L19-023, S-L19-033, S-L19-032, S-L19-025, S-L19-024

### STD-enter-exit-origin-06: Exit the way it entered
**must**. Make an element leave along the same path and edge it entered from, with its swipe-to-dismiss direction matching that entrance: a toast or panel that slides in from the bottom or right dismisses to the bottom or right. The web recipes express this by giving the entrance and the exit one shared state ([data-starting-style], [data-ending-style]).
- Why: Symmetric paths create spatial consistency and are what make swipe-to-dismiss feel obvious; entering from one edge and leaving to another reads as two unrelated elements.
- Sources: S-L19-018, S-L19-020, S-L19-015, S-L19-023, S-L19-024, S-L19-012, S-L19-017

### STD-enter-exit-origin-08: Dropdowns and popovers: scale 0.95, 200ms
**must** · web, css, react. Enter and exit dropdowns, popovers, menus and selects between opacity: 0 plus a slightly smaller scale (recipe: scale(0.95)) and their resting state, transitioning opacity and transform together within 150–250ms (recipe: 200ms) on the strong ease-out curve.
- Values: start-and-end-opacity: 0; start-and-end-scale: 0.95; duration: 200ms; duration-range: 150–250ms; easing: cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1); states: [data-starting-style], [data-ending-style]
- Why: The panel scales out of its trigger, not out of thin air, and a short duration keeps it responsive: a 180ms dropdown feels more responsive than a 400ms one.
- `engine.py review` checks it: Time dropdowns, popovers, menus and selects with the motion.duration.medium token (var(--ds-motion-duration-medium)); the house budget is 150 to 250 milliseconds.
- Sources: S-L19-017, S-L19-018, S-L19-033, S-L19-025, S-L19-024, S-L19-023, S-L19-003, S-L19-012, S-L19-004

### STD-enter-exit-origin-09: Tooltips: scale 0.97, 125ms
**must** · web, css, react. Enter and exit tooltips between opacity: 0 + transform: scale(0.97) and their resting state, scaling from the trigger (transform-origin: var(--transform-origin)), in 125ms on the ease-out curve; tooltips and small popovers stay within 125–200ms.
- Values: start-and-end-opacity: 0; start-and-end-scale: 0.97; duration: 125ms; duration-range: 125–200ms; easing: cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1); transform-origin: var(--transform-origin); transition: transform 125ms var(--ease-out), opacity 125ms var(--ease-out)
- Why: A tooltip is the same shape as a popover, only faster.
- Sources: S-L19-017, S-L19-003, S-L19-023, S-L19-018, S-L19-033, S-L19-025, S-L19-024

### STD-enter-exit-origin-10: Delay only the first tooltip
**must** · web, css, react. Give the first tooltip in a group a delay before it appears, then open neighbouring tooltips instantly with no delay and no animation while one is open (Base UI: transition-duration: 0ms on [data-instant]).
- Values: subsequent-tooltip-transition-duration: 0ms; selector: .tooltip[data-instant]
- Why: The initial delay prevents accidental activation; skipping both the delay and the animation afterwards makes the whole toolbar feel faster without defeating the purpose of the delay.
- Sources: S-L19-003, S-L19-012, S-L19-004, S-L19-017, S-L19-023, S-L19-033, S-L19-025

### STD-enter-exit-origin-11: Modals: centered scale 0.96, 250ms
**must** · web, css, react. Enter and exit modals between opacity: 0 plus a slightly smaller scale (recipe: scale(0.96)) and their resting state, kept centered, within 200–500ms (recipe: 250ms) on the ease-out curve.
- Values: start-and-end-opacity: 0; start-and-end-scale: 0.96; duration: 250ms; duration-range: 200–500ms; article-duration-range: 200-300ms (Agents with taste); easing: cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1); transform-origin: center
- Why: The modal is the one popover that stays centered, because it is not anchored to a trigger; the duration tables give modals and drawers 200–500ms, and the modal recipe uses 250ms.
- Sources: S-L19-017, S-L19-018, S-L19-033, S-L19-025, S-L19-024, S-L19-023, S-L19-004

### STD-enter-exit-origin-12: Fade the backdrop with the modal
**should** · web, css, react. Pair a modal with a dimming backdrop and transition the backdrop's opacity alongside the modal with the same timing (opacity 250ms on the ease-out curve).
- Values: backdrop-transition: opacity 250ms var(--ease-out)
- Why: Animating the backdrop's opacity with the modal makes them read as one surface; a modal task pairs the surface with a dimming scrim.
- Sources: S-L19-017, S-L19-020, S-L19-018, S-L19-033

### STD-enter-exit-origin-13: Stagger group entrances 30–80ms
**must**. When several items enter together (a list or grid seen occasionally, STD-when-to-animate-13), stagger them by 30–80ms each instead of bringing everything in at once (web recipe: each item from opacity: 0 and translateY(8px) over 300ms ease-out, delays 0, 50, 100, 150ms; React Native recipe: FadeInDown.duration(250).delay(index * 40)).
- Values: step-range: 30–80ms; web-recipe-step: 50ms; web-recipe-delays: 0ms, 50ms, 100ms, 150ms; item-start: opacity: 0; transform: translateY(8px); item-duration: 300ms; item-easing: ease-out (var(--ease-out)); react-native-recipe: FadeInDown.duration(250).delay(index * 40)
- Why: A cascade feels more natural than everything appearing at once; longer delays make the interface feel slow, and shorter ones read as simultaneous.
- `engine.py review` checks it: Keep each stagger step between 30 and 80 milliseconds per item: use the motion.duration.stagger token (var(--ds-motion-duration-stagger)); Motion's stagger() takes seconds.
- Sources: S-L19-018, S-L19-017, S-L19-023, S-L19-033, S-L19-032, S-L19-025, S-L19-024, S-L19-015

### STD-enter-exit-origin-16: Bridge appearing and disappearing content
**should**. Give content that appears, vanishes or swaps (conditional renders, route content, expanding sections, toasts) a short enter and exit transition instead of letting it pop in or out, unless the frequency rules say not to animate it at all.
- Values: entrance: scale(0.95–0.97) + opacity: 0, ease-out
- Why: Elements appearing or disappearing without a transition feel broken; preventing a jarring change is a valid purpose for motion.
- Sources: S-L19-023, S-L19-024, S-L19-025, S-L19-012

### STD-enter-exit-origin-17: Use @starting-style for mount entry
**should** · web, css, react. Animate an element's entry on mount with CSS @starting-style where browser support allows, and fall back to a data-mounted attribute set to true in a useEffect after the first render.
- Values: css: @starting-style { opacity: 0; transform: ... }; fallback: useEffect(() => { setMounted(true); }, []); <div data-mounted={mounted}>
- Why: @starting-style animates entry without JavaScript and replaces the useEffect mounted-flag pattern, which still works everywhere.
- Sources: S-L19-018, S-L19-023, S-L19-033, S-L19-025, S-L19-024, S-L19-017, S-L19-006

### STD-enter-exit-origin-21: Slide by percentages, not pixels
**should** · web, css, react-native. When an element slides fully in or out by its own size (a toast, drawer or sheet), express the distance as a percentage of that size, such as translateY(100%), rather than a hardcoded pixel offset. Small nudges stay in pixels in the recipes (the stagger's translateY(8px), the collapsing header's -12).
- Values: example: translateY(100%)
- Why: Percentages in translate() are relative to the element's own size, so translateY(100%) moves it by its own height whatever the content; this is how Sonner positions toasts and Vaul hides a drawer.
- `engine.py review` checks it: Hide toasts and drawers with translateY(100%), which follows the element's own size, not a fixed pixel offset.
- Sources: S-L19-018, S-L19-023, S-L19-033, S-L19-025, S-L19-024, S-L19-016

### STD-enter-exit-origin-23: Accordions: short height and opacity
**must** · web, css, react. Animate accordions and collapses with overflow: hidden and a short height plus opacity transition (recipe: height 200ms and opacity 200ms on the ease-out curve).
- Values: properties: height, opacity; duration: 200ms; easing: cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1); overflow: hidden
- Why: An accordion that snaps open needs a transition, but it is one of the few animations that costs layout on every frame, so a long duration is expensive as well as sluggish.
- Sources: S-L19-017, S-L19-024

### STD-enter-exit-origin-24: Measure heights, never animate to auto
**must** · web, react, react-native, ios, android, css. Measure the content height before animating a collapse or expansion, and never animate to a hardcoded height (React Native) or to auto (web): measure with onLayout in React Native, and in JavaScript or through a headless primitive that supplies it on the web; or animate a transform instead.
- Values: measure-react-native: onLayout; font-scale: 200%; never-animate-to: auto (web), a hardcoded height (React Native)
- Why: In React Native allowFontScaling is on by default, so a height measured at the default text size is wrong at 200%; on the web the accordion recipe measures the content height rather than animating to auto.
- `engine.py review` checks it: Animating height to a fixed number breaks when text scales; measure with onLayout or animate a transform.
- Sources: S-L19-017, S-L19-016

### STD-enter-exit-origin-25: React Native: never animate header height
**must** · react-native, ios, android. In React Native, never animate height to collapse or reveal anything, a header on scroll least of all: give the container a fixed height, translate the content inside it and clip with overflow: 'hidden'. The only element the source lets animate a layout property is an absolutely positioned one with no children, such as a tab pill or progress fill.
- Values: collapse-recipe: opacity 1 → 0 and translateY 0 → -12 over scroll 0 → 60, Extrapolation.CLAMP; large-title: headerLargeTitleEnabled (iOS only)
- Why: Animating height runs a layout pass on the header and everything below it on every scroll frame, the one animation guaranteed to stutter because it competes with the scroll; width, height, margin, padding, flex, top and left re-run Yoga for the node and its siblings on every frame.
- `engine.py review` checks it: Don't animate height in React Native: translate the content inside a fixed-height, overflow-hidden container (only absolute, childless elements are exempt).
- Sources: S-L19-015, S-L19-016

### STD-enter-exit-origin-26: Reveal with clip-path inset
**should** · web, css, react. Reveal or hide part of an element (images, scroll reveals, comparison sliders) by animating clip-path: inset(), from inset(0 0 100% 0) to inset(0 0 0 0) on the ease-in-out curve, not by animating width, height or an overflow-hidden wrapper.
- Values: hidden: clip-path: inset(0 0 100% 0); shown: clip-path: inset(0 0 0 0); easing: cubic-bezier(0.77, 0, 0.175, 1); scroll-reveal-duration: 600ms; image-reveal-duration: 1000ms (1s); comparison-slider: clip-path: inset(0 50% 0 0)
- Why: clip-path is hardware-accelerated, needs no extra DOM elements and causes no layout shift when the image is revealed.
- Sources: S-L19-010, S-L19-017, S-L19-018, S-L19-033, S-L19-025, S-L19-023

### STD-enter-exit-origin-27: Scroll reveals on marketing pages only
**must** · web. Use scroll-triggered reveals only on marketing surfaces, never on functional UI a user visits daily.
- Why: The recipe limits scroll reveals to marketing surfaces; a surface visited daily falls under the frequency gate, where repeated motion makes the interface feel slow, and data the user reads or acts on should not move for style.
- Sources: S-L19-017, S-L19-024

### STD-enter-exit-origin-28: Fire scroll reveals once, 100px in
**must** · web, react. Trigger a scroll reveal when the element enters the viewport and fire it only once (IntersectionObserver, or Motion's useInView with { once: true, margin: "-100px" }, which fires once at least 100px of the element is in view).
- Values: useInView: { once: true, margin: "-100px" }
- Why: The reveal must run where the user can see it, or they never see it animate; re-animating on every scroll-by is an interface fighting its reader.
- Sources: S-L19-017, S-L19-010

### STD-enter-exit-origin-29: Blur a crossfade that won't settle
**must** · web, css, react. When a crossfade still shows two overlapping states after you have tried other easings and durations, add filter: blur(2px) during the transition (recipe: opacity 0.7, filter and opacity over 200ms ease).
- Values: blur: 2px; opacity-during: 0.7; duration: 200ms; easing: ease
- Why: Without blur the eye reads two distinct objects swapping; blur blends them into one perceived transformation.
- Sources: S-L19-003, S-L19-017, S-L19-023, S-L19-033, S-L19-032, S-L19-025

### STD-enter-exit-origin-30: Keep animated blur under 20px
**must** · web, css, react. Keep any animated or transition-time blur() under 20px.
- Values: max-animated-blur: under 20px
- Why: Heavy blur is expensive, especially in Safari, and causes performance issues.
- `engine.py review` checks it: Keep animated blur under 20px (the crossfade mask uses 2px).
- Sources: S-L19-013, S-L19-017, S-L19-023, S-L19-033, S-L19-025, S-L19-004

### STD-enter-exit-origin-31: Materialize glass surfaces, don't fade
**should**. When a glass or blurred surface enters or exits, animate its blur radius and scale together rather than using a plain opacity fade.
- Why: The surface then reads as a real material arriving rather than a plain opacity fade.
- Sources: S-L19-020

### STD-enter-exit-origin-33: No entering on virtualized rows
**must** · react-native, ios, android. Never put an entering animation on a row inside FlatList, FlashList or any virtualized list; animate the list container once on mount, or use itemLayoutAnimation for reflow only.
- Why: Rows are recycled, so the animation re-fires every time one scrolls back into view and the list appears to flicker while the user scrolls.
- `engine.py review` checks it: No entering on virtualized list rows: animate the container once, or use itemLayoutAnimation for reflow.
- Sources: S-L19-015, S-L19-016

### STD-enter-exit-origin-34: The list closes a removed row's gap
**should** · react-native. When a row is removed, let the list close the gap with itemLayoutAnimation={LinearTransition.duration(200)}, the builder defined at module scope, rather than animating the row.
- Values: itemLayoutAnimation: LinearTransition.duration(200)
- Why: Closing the gap the deleted row left is the list's job, not the row's.
- Sources: S-L19-015

### STD-enter-exit-origin-35: Layout animations for mount and unmount
**should** · react-native. In React Native, animate elements mounting or unmounting and lists reflowing with Reanimated layout animations (entering, exiting, itemLayoutAnimation).
- Why: The animate-expo tool table, walked from the top to the cheapest tool that fits, assigns mounting, unmounting and list reflow to layout animations.
- Sources: S-L19-016

### STD-enter-exit-origin-37: Tune opacity against height by eye
**should**. When items enter or exit a list with a height change (including reflowing toast stacks), tune the opacity change against the height animation by eye and check it again the next day.
- Why: The opacity change has to work with the height change and there is no formula for that pair; imperfections show up with fresh eyes.
- Sources: S-L19-023, S-L19-017, S-L19-033, S-L19-015

### STD-enter-exit-origin-38: Set every transform-origin on purpose
**should** · web, css. Check the transform-origin of every scaled or rotated element, SVG elements included, and set it to where the motion should grow from instead of relying on the default; verify it in slow motion.
- Why: Every element transforms from an anchor point whose default is center, and slow-motion review checks whether an element scales from the wrong point.
- Sources: S-L19-023, S-L19-033, S-L19-031, S-L19-001

### STD-enter-exit-origin-39: Mirror easing on reversible transitions
**should**. On a reversible transition, mirror the easing so the outbound path matches the return path (inverse cubic-bézier control points for the two directions); for UI entrances and exits the ease-out rule (STD-easing-duration-01) still applies, since the inverse of an ease-out is an ease-in [inferred].
- Why: Apple: if something disappears one way, we expect it to emerge from where it came.
- Sources: S-L19-020

### STD-enter-exit-origin-40: Vaul: --initial-transform off the edge
**should** · web, react, css. When a Vaul side drawer does not touch the screen edge, adjust its enter and exit animation with the --initial-transform CSS variable.
- Values: css-variable: --initial-transform
- Why: The Vaul docs name --initial-transform as the way to adjust the animation when the drawer does not touch the edge. Vaul is good-to-have only: its README says the library is unmaintained (learn/sources.json, checked 2026-09-24).
- Sources: S-L19-094

### STD-enter-exit-origin-41: Drawers: 500ms on the drawer curve
**should** · web, css, react. Hide a drawer or sheet at transform: translateY(100%) and open and close it with transition: transform 500ms var(--ease-drawer), where --ease-drawer is cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1); once a drag is involved it becomes a gesture and settles with a spring instead.
- Values: closed: [data-closed] { transform: translateY(100%) }; open: transform: translateY(0); transition: transform 500ms var(--ease-drawer); --ease-drawer: cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1); article: transition: transform 0.5s cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1)
- Why: The curve closely matches iOS (it comes from the Ionic Framework) and 500ms is meant to mimic iOS's sheet; translateY(100%) hides the drawer by its own height whatever its content, which is how Vaul hides a drawer before animating it in.
- Sources: S-L19-017, S-L19-005, S-L19-018, S-L19-023

### STD-enter-exit-origin-42: Tab color changes: clip a duplicate
**should** · web, css, react. When the active tab has a different background or text color, show the change by duplicating the tab list, styling the copy as the active state, clipping the copy with clip-path: inset() so only the active tab shows (measured from the active tab's offsetLeft and offsetWidth, rounded with inset(... round r)), and animating that clip on change; do not time individual text-color transitions across the tabs.
- Values: active-copy-clip: clip-path: inset(0 <right>% 0 <left>% round <radius>) from the active tab's offsetLeft / offsetWidth (article example: inset(0px 75% 0px 0% round 17px)); transition: clip-path 250ms var(--ease-in-out); accessibility: the copy is aria-hidden with tabIndex={-1} buttons (STD-accessibility-motion-17); the real tabs sit on an accessible primitive such as Radix Tabs (STD-accessibility-motion-16)
- Why: The text and background change together in perfect sync because one element is revealed rather than two colors being interpolated; a text-color transition is only okay-ish and can never be timed to be seamless.
- Sources: S-L19-010, S-L19-017, S-L19-023

### STD-enter-exit-origin-43: Scroll-linked reveals map progress to clip-path
**should** · web, react. Drive a reveal that follows scroll position (such as a line that grows as the page scrolls) from a scroll-progress motion value mapped onto clip-path: useScroll({ target, offset: ["start end", "end end"] }), then useTransform(scrollYProgress, [0, 1], ["100%", "0%"]), then useMotionTemplate`inset(0 0 ${clipPathY} 0)` applied as an inline clip-path style, keeping each step a motion value rather than saving it in a plain variable.
- Values: offset: ["start end", "end end"]; mapping: useTransform(scrollYProgress, [0, 1], ["100%", "0%"]); style: useMotionTemplate`inset(0 0 ${clipPathY} 0)` as an inline clip-path style; surface: scroll-driven reveals belong on marketing surfaces (STD-enter-exit-origin-27) [inferred]
- Why: The offset starts measuring when the element's top reaches the bottom of the viewport and stops when its bottom does, so the animation is not reverted when the user scrolls past it. A motion value holds the up-to-date value without re-rendering the component and updates automatically when used as an inline style; a value saved in a plain variable would not receive updates.
- Sources: S-L19-010

### STD-enter-exit-origin-44: Theme-switch reveals use View Transitions
**should** · web, css. Build a theme-switch reveal, where one theme uncovers the other through an animated clip-path, with the View Transitions API instead of duplicating the whole page or element and clipping the copy.
- Values: technique: animate clip-path to reveal the other theme; avoid: a duplicated page or element per theme
- Why: Duplicating the element to animate is hacky and was only fine for a quick prototype; the View Transitions API achieves the same effect without the duplicate.
- Sources: S-L19-010
